title: A Goldman Economist Says AI Will Take 15 Years to Show Up in the Economy. A 63-Year-Old Banking His Nest Egg on the AI Boom Should Listen.
excerpt: Goldman Sachs says AI could take 15 years to move the economic needle, but millions of near-retirees are already betting their nest eggs on the boom arriving...
content_html:
Gerelyn Terzo

Tue, July 28, 2026 at 10:01 AM MST 6 min read

Quick Read

  • A Goldman Sachs economist warns AI productivity gains could take 15 years to register in economic data, making AI-driven retirement math unreliable.

  • Delaying Social Security from 62 to 70 raises monthly benefits from roughly $1,680 to $2,976, which amounts to a $15,000-per-year gap indexed to inflation for life.

  • Sequence-of-returns risk permanently shrinks portfolios when retirees withdraw during downturns. Holding one to three years of expenses in cash neutralizes that threat.

  • Two retirees, same $1 million, same 4% rule, buy one finished with $1.4 million, the other hit $0 in 12 years. Our free reader guide explains the flaw that separated them, and the income-first method built to avoid it.

Picture a 63-year-old sitting at the kitchen table with his 401(k) statement. He is two years from Medicare, maybe four from claiming Social Security, and his retirement math looks great. The S&P 500 is up about 20% over the past year and roughly 72% over five years. If that pace continues at even half speed, with AI powering the markets, he retires comfortably.

That if is doing a lot of work. A Goldman Sachs economist offered a reality check on AI adoption: it took roughly 15 years for computers to meaningfully show up in the economic data, and current AI rollout is gradual and uneven despite the hype about replacing white-collar work. The productivity payoff may still arrive. It may not arrive on his retirement timeline.

The current data supports the caution. Goldman's own research found no meaningful relationship between AI adoption and productivity at the economy-wide level, and fewer than 20% of U.S. businesses are using AI for any function at all. Nothing in the economic numbers screams productivity revolution. Versions of this exact worry appear on retirement forums lately, with near-retirees asking whether to keep riding the tech rally or lock in what they have.

The 4% Rule is Broken, Built On A World That No Longer Exists

Every retiree knows about the 4% rule, but it frames retirement as a slow liquidation and still causes retirees with seven-figure accounts to agonize over a dinner out.

There's a different way to run the math that makes more sense today. Build an income floor — dividends, interest, and Social Security that cover your essential bills every month — and you never have to sell shares into a down market just to pay them.

Our free reader guide, The 4% Rule Is Broken, walks through it in about 15 minutes. Access the report here.

快速阅读

  • 高盛经济学家警告称，人工智能生产率的提高可能需要 15 年才能体现在经济数据中，这使得人工智能驱动的退休数学变得不可靠。
  • 将社会保障从 62 岁推迟到 70 岁，每月福利从大约 1,680 美元增加到 2,976 美元，相当于终身通货膨胀导致每年 15,000 美元的缺口。
  • 当退休人员在经济低迷时期退出时，回报序列风险会永久缩小投资组合。 持有一到三年的现金支出可以抵消这种威胁。
  • 两名退休人员，同样的 100 万美元，同样的 4% 规则，买了一个最终以 140 万美元完成，另一个在 12 年内跌至 0 美元。 我们的免费读者指南解释了将他们分开的缺陷，以及为避免该缺陷而建立的收入优先方法。

想象一下一位 63 岁的老人坐在厨房的桌子旁，拿着他的 401(k) 声明。 他还有两年的时间享受医疗保险，也许还有四年的时间领取社会保障，而且他的退休数学看起来很棒。 标准普尔 500 指数在过去一年上涨了约 20%，在五年内上涨了约 72%。 如果这种速度继续保持一半的速度，并且人工智能为市场提供动力，他就会轻松退休。

如果要做很多工作。 高盛的一位经济学家对人工智能的采用进行了现实检验：计算机花了大约 15 年的时间才有意义地出现在经济数据中，尽管人们大肆宣传要取代白领工作，但目前人工智能的推广是渐进且不平衡的。 生产力的回报可能仍然会到来。 它可能不会在他的退休时间表上到来。

当前的数据支持了这种谨慎态度。 高盛自己的研究发现，人工智能的采用与整个经济层面的生产力之间没有有意义的关系，只有不到 20% 的美国企业在任何功能上使用人工智能。 经济数据中没有任何东西能够引发生产力革命。 最近，退休论坛上出现了这种担忧的不同版本，即将退休的人询问是否继续搭乘科技股的涨势，还是锁定他们所拥有的东西。

4% 规则被打破，建立在一个不再存在的世界上

每个退休人员都知道 4% 的规则，但它将退休视为一种缓慢的清算，并且仍然导致拥有七位数账户的退休人员为外出就餐而苦恼。

今天有一种更有意义的不同的数学计算方法。 建立一个收入底线——股息、利息和社会保障，足以支付你每月的基本账单——你永远不需要在低迷的市场上出售股票来支付这些费用。

我们的免费读者指南《4% 规则被打破》大约需要 15 分钟。 在此访问报告。
